title: Round 7 / ECDLP-22: novelty settlement for Theorems A/B and fresh high-risk hypotheses
question: (a) Retrieve and compare Lange–Winterhof / Kiltz–Winterhof / Shparlinski results on interpolation of the EC discrete logarithm with Theorems A/B (exact statements). (b) Independently generate 3-5 new, testable, high-risk hypotheses toward faster ECDLP that do NOT reduce to: homomorphic transfer, summation-polynomial index calculus, cover-based Jacobians, coordinate-predicate bias, or algebraic interpolation (all already investigated), each with mechanism, obligations, invalidators and cheapest decisive test; run the cheapest test for the most promising one.

claims: Part (a): no exact statement of Lange-Winterhof, Kiltz-Winterhof or Shparlinski was accessible (abstract-level only). Theorem A is known in kind (published ECDL interpolation degree lower bounds; Satoh 2005 refines them); exact relation unsettled. Theorem B: not found in accessible material; overlap plausible; novelty unsettled.
Part (b): five speculative hypotheses D1-D5; none claims an ECDLP speed-up. D4 coincides with the xedni-calculus literature; D5 reduces to D1.

Experimental (toy, p<=211, seed 7, 50 curve/map rows): d*(phi_m)=M-c+1 in all rows, no violation of the bound d*>=M/m^2, same as random permutations of equal cycle type; D1 supported under the pre-registered rule. Evidence level: experimental, finite domain.
next_action: Obtain LNCS 2387/2643 full texts via library and compare Theorems A/B by hand; optionally extend D1 test to rational class functions.
